units.title: C1 compact functions lie in the same closed gradient graph

sources.label: PBPS Appendix C.1 omitted analytic domain prerequisite
sources.scope: Same actual compact-gradient graph closure admits C1 compact function/gradient pairs; actual positive-epsilon weak resolvent has all C1 compact weighted volume tests and genuine ordinary weak gradient. Actual PBPS reflected conditional R/S law and original fixed D precede epsilon/input. No local H2, global operator-core/Bochner, conditional Poincare/BL, centered epsilon limit, noncompact constant/linear domains, measurable y-selection, SPHMC Hessian lower/full4.1, PBPS hypocoercivity or either complete main/composition. TV never transfers unbounded expected cost.

assumptions: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with Borel measurable structure and canonical volume, including dimension zero. mu is any finite measure; no absolute-continuity or Gibbs hypothesis on mu is required.

D is the same closable real-linear partial operator, with original graph iff actual C-infinity compact scalar representatives and their genuine gradients, both classes identified mu-a.e. This semantics comes from the existing gradient producer in the paper consumer.
The tested scalar f is only C1 and compactly supported. Its gradient, L2 integrability and actual closure membership are conclusions, not inputs.
units.statement: For every finite Borel measure mu, every closable partial gradient D whose original graph is exactly compact smooth scalar representatives and their genuine gradients, and every C1 compact scalar f, derive MemLp f 2 mu and MemLp (gradient f) 2 mu and prove the actual pair of their L2 classes lies in D.closure.graph. No graph-membership or approximation certificate is supplied.

steps.title: Construct genuine normalized compact mollifiers
steps.text: Choose bump radii (n+1)^-1 and twice that value. Normalize the actual smooth compact nonnegative kernel against canonical volume; it has integral one and shrinking support. The approximation is the real convolution g_n=rho_n*f, not a supplied approximating sequence.

steps.title: Differentiate the actual convolution
steps.text: Compact support and C1 regularity justify the right-variable derivative theorem. Actual g_n is compact smooth and its Frechet derivative is convolution with Df. This establishes a joint function/derivative sequence.

steps.title: Derive both squared L2 limits from bounded domination
steps.text: Compact continuous f and its continuous compact derivative have bounded norms C and B. Kernel positivity/mass one bounds each convolution by the same constant. Pointwise mollifier convergence plus the integrable constant (2C)^2 or (2B)^2 under finite mu gives both genuine squared-error integral limits. No uniform-convergence or common-support premise is needed in this finite-measure argument.

steps.title: Convert derivative and integral convergence into true L2 topology
steps.text: The Riesz isometry identifies gradient with the actual Frechet derivative and preserves norms of differences. The L2 inner-product norm formula identifies norm difference with square root of the actual squared-error integral. Both genuine L2 classes converge jointly.

steps.title: Use the original graph and its actual closure
steps.text: Each pair belongs to the original exact compact smooth gradient graph by its representatives. Its joint L2 limit lies in the closed topological graph closure. Actual closability identifies that closure with D.closure.graph; the same operator is preserved.

steps.title: Keep the analytic boundary explicit
steps.text: This derives C1 compact domain membership only. Noncompact constants/linear observables still need true tail cutoffs; local H2 and the generator core/global Bochner are separate. Zero dimension is included without a unit-vector assumption.
steps.formula: C_c^1\subset\operatorname{dom}\overline D;\quad H^2,\ D^*D\text{ core},\ \mathrm{BL}\text{ remain open}.
